commit.message:
Pin Coston2 on every write so a wrong-network send is impossible

createPublicInvoice failed with "RPC 0x1 Infura eth_sendRawTransaction: gas
required exceeds allowance (0)". Both wallets hold C2FLR on Coston2, so it was
not a funding problem: 0x1 is Ethereum mainnet. The wallet was on mainnet, the
accounts have no ETH there, and mainnet's RPC refused to estimate gas.

None of the writeContract calls specified a chainId, so wagmi broadcast to
whatever chain the wallet was on. RequireWallet only gates rendering, which is
not the same as gating the send. Every write and the quote simulation now pin
chainId: coston2.id, so wagmi raises ChainMismatchError before broadcasting.

explainError also translates the two symptoms — the mismatch itself and the
gas-estimation failure it produces — into a message naming Coston2 and chain
114, instead of surfacing raw RPC text. Two tests cover the exact strings.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Make invoice records publicly viewable and add demo seeding

Two things blocked a reviewer from evaluating the app.

1. /invoices/[id] was wrapped in RequireWallet, so following a link showed a
   connect-wallet prompt instead of the record. Everything that page renders is
   public on-chain state, so the gate was wrong: it now reads the chain directly
   and only the settlement actions ask for a signer. A judge can open an invoice
   link and see the seller, buyer, total, commitment and status immediately.

2. The escrow had no invoices at all (nextInvoiceId == 1), so the app was empty.
   scripts/seed-demo-invoice.ts creates a real public-fallback invoice, printing
   the id, the explorer link and the app links. It uses createPublicInvoice and
   labels the result as such — it does not stand in for a confidential invoice.

Also adds a vector redraw of the existing brand mark (public/mark.svg,
public/logo.svg, app/icon.svg). The repo previously had only a 1 MB PNG and no
favicon; the SVG is ~1 KB, stays crisp at 16px, and keeps the same identity
rather than introducing a competing one.

commit.message:
Add the live app link to README and SUBMISSION

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Deploy to Vercel and gate the confidential flow on the real TEE state

Live at https://flareseal.vercel.app

Fixes a bug the deployment surfaced: the landing page reported "Confidential
mode: Available" whenever an InstructionSender address was configured, ignoring
whether the escrow actually has a TEE signer. It does not — teeAddress is still
zero — so "Create private invoice" was enabled on a path that cannot complete.
A user would have encrypted their invoice, paid gas for the instruction
transaction, waited out the poll timeout, and only then hit TeeNotConfigured.

useConfidentialAvailable now reads teeAddress() from the deployed escrow and
requires it to be non-zero. The badge reads "Awaiting TEE", the submit button is
disabled, and the form explains why rather than failing late and expensively.

.env.production holds only public on-chain addresses and is committed
deliberately: NEXT_PUBLIC_* are inlined at build time, so Vercel needs them
present or it bakes in "not configured". FCC_PROXY_URL is deliberately absent —
the TEE stack is local, so /api/fcc/* correctly returns 503 and the UI shows the
extension-unavailable state instead of hanging.

Verified live: all five routes 200, both API routes degrade correctly, and the
page reads teeAddress from Coston2 on load.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Deploy FlareSealInstructionSender and register the FCC extension on Coston2

InstructionSender: 0xF7F75FF93B500f7199E200Cb665A9573A2b73897
Extension ID:      0x...0101ac (65964)
Registry:          0x1a9C4A0f9D76c0b1D91d22E24E573a9b377618aE

Verified independently against the chain rather than trusting the script: 2186
bytes of code at the address, OP_TYPE_INVOICE = "INVOICE" and
OP_COMMAND_CREATE = "CREATE" read back from the deployed contract. Those match
the TypeScript extension's constants, which the build prompt calls out as a
must-match invariant.

Reaching this took fixing the pre-flight failure described in the previous
commit; the deployment itself then went through unmodified scaffold tooling.

Still outstanding: teeAddress, which can only come from the proxy /info endpoint
and therefore still waits on the Coston2 indexer DB.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Normalize remaining CRLF files and skip redundant binding regeneration

check-versions.sh failed the pre-flight with a "tee-proxy mismatch" between
v0.0.18 and v0.0.18. bash -x showed why: TOOLS_PROXY=$'v0.0.18\r' — tools/go.mod
was still CRLF, so the string compare failed against a value that displayed
identically. Same root cause as the conformance and shebang failures; go.mod,
go.sum, *.go, *.toml and *.example were outside the first normalization pass and
are now covered, matching .gitattributes.

generate-bindings.sh now skips abigen when both autogen.go files are newer than
their contract sources. go:generate shells out to `go run .../cmd/abigen`, which
compiles go-ethereum from source on a cold cache — minutes on a local disk and
far worse over a /mnt/c bind mount — and pre-build.sh calls it on every run.
FORCE_BINDINGS=1 overrides.

Pre-flight now reports all version pins consistent.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Record conformance results and the real FCC blocker

Conformance now genuinely passes 15/15, and the guard was verified by watching
it fail: with the fixture paths still broken all 15 reported "unreadable by jq"
rather than passing.

Docker turned out to be present after all — Engine 29.6.1 and Compose v5.3.1
inside WSL Ubuntu, dockerd running, reachable as root without elevation. Three
environment faults were blocking it (CRLF scripts, hard Foundry dependency,
stale documented lifecycle), all now fixed.

The genuine blocker is one step further in: the Coston2 ext-proxy requires a
chain indexer DB on MySQL 3306 whose credentials are placeholders in the
scaffold, and whose compose service lives in a different Flare repository that
is not vendored here. That needs either Flare-operated indexer credentials or a
locally synced Coston2 indexer.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add submission doc, pin line endings, and drop the hard Foundry dependency

.gitattributes pins LF for shell scripts, Dockerfiles, YAML and Python. On
Windows core.autocrlf=true rewrote every FCC script on checkout, so bash in
WSL and in containers rejected them with:

    /usr/bin/env: 'bash\r': No such file or directory

That made the whole FCC pipeline unrunnable on this platform regardless of
whether Docker was present.

generate-bindings.sh now falls back to the Hardhat artifact when forge is
absent, using the hardhat.fcc.config.ts path that already exists for exactly
this case. forge remains preferred when installed.

SUBMISSION.md answers the program's submission questions from the real build,
and marks the two fields only the team can supply (bounty selection, demo
video).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Rewrite conformance fixtures for INVOICE/CREATE and make the suite able to fail

The fixtures were still the scaffold's Hello World set (GREETING/SAY_HELLO)
while the extension registers INVOICE/CREATE, and two bugs meant the suite
reported "16 passed" without asserting anything:

1. Windows jq.exe emits CRLF, so `read -r name` left a trailing CR inside the
   fixture path ("...-payload\r.json") and every open failed.
2. On a jq failure the expected/actual pair were both empty, compared equal,
   and each `jq -e 'has(...)'` probe exited non-zero so the assertion blocks
   were skipped as "not requested" — scoring the case green.

Fixes: strip CR in both jq-fed read loops, and fail loudly on any fixture jq
cannot read. Verified the guard works — with the paths broken all 15 fixtures
now FAIL rather than silently pass.

New fixtures cover the three pre-decryption rejection paths, the rejection
counter, every framework status code (501/400/405/404), a regression case
asserting GREETING no longer routes, and a privacy guard that reported state
carries counters only. A success case is deliberately absent: INVOICE/CREATE
decrypts through tee-node's sign port, which the harness does not run, and
faking it would stop testing the wire contract. Handler success stays covered
by the vitest suite via setDecryptor.

gen_fixtures.py no longer needs eth_abi and now prunes stale fixtures.

15/15 passing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Record FCC conformance and Go tooling test findings

The conformance suite reports "16 passed" on this machine but asserts nothing:
jq cannot open fixture paths containing a space, and the script compares two
empty strings on jq failure, scoring it as a pass. Separately the fixtures are
still the scaffold's Hello World set (GREETING/SAY_HELLO) while the extension
now registers INVOICE/CREATE, so those cases should fail.

Also records the one Go tooling failure, TestSaveState_ReadOnlyDir, which is
upstream and Windows-specific: Windows ACLs do not enforce a read-only
directory against the owning user.

Neither originates in FlareSeal code. Documented rather than left as a
misleading green result.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Deploy FlareSealEscrow to Coston2

Escrow live at 0xEe7aDeb4268CDC40F3138F7caF08432A1433F204
tx 0x1e022add9356a631382b19f344f4f4c96489cc0d20bd66caf1207d94b5e5acf1

FXRP and FTSOv2 were resolved through the Contract Registry and the FAssets
Asset Manager rather than hardcoded. Every immutable was read back off the
deployed contract and matched; verified independently with both smoke scripts.
A live FTSOv2 read returned XRP/USD 1.067628 at age 0s.

teeAddress is deliberately still zero — it can only come from the FCC proxy
/info endpoint, which needs the Docker stack. relayConfidentialInvoice reverts
with TeeNotConfigured until then, which is the correct refusal to accept an
unverifiable result.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

FlareSeal: confidential invoices with FXRP escrow on Coston2

Invoice line items, customer identities, and tax details are encrypted in
the browser and validated inside a Flare Confidential Compute TEE. Only the
parties, USD total, due date, and a terms commitment reach the chain.

- contracts/: FlareSealEscrow with TEE-signature relay, replay protection,
  FTSOv2 pricing with staleness bounds, and no owner path to escrowed funds.
  72 tests, 100% statement coverage.
- fcc/: TypeScript INVOICE/CREATE extension on the official scaffold, with
  bigint-only arithmetic and a deterministic terms commitment. 91 tests.
- web/: Next.js app covering the full confidential creation state machine,
  FXRP approval/funding/release, and FTSOv2 quoting. 83 tests.

Not yet deployed: no deployer key and no Docker runtime available. No TEE
signature is faked and no FCC assertion is stubbed; see BUILD_REPORT.md.
